title: Phase locking nuclear spins in silicon with spin-orbit coupling
authors: Habitamu Y. Walelign, Manas Ranjan Sahu, John M. Nichol
abstract: Because they have such long coherence times, nuclear spins have extraordinary potential for use in quantum information processing devices. However, coherent nuclear spin control generally requires external phase references, such as microwave control fields. Here, we phase-lock a $^{29}$Si nuclear spin ensemble in a silicon quantum dot using only the internal electronic spin-orbit coupling as a phase reference. When driven with the quantum-dot electrons, the nuclear spins align themselves to a phase determined by the electronic spin-orbit coupling and the timing of the drive protocol. This enables us to measure the coherent precession and inhomogeneous dephasing of the nuclear spins. We corroborate our results with detailed numerical simulations of the many-body electron nuclear system. Our work opens new routes for coherently controlling solid-state nuclear spin ensembles.
summary: The research demonstrates a novel method to coherently control nuclear spins in silicon quantum dots by leveraging the internal spin-orbit coupling (SOC). By engineering specific pulse sequences that induce dynamic nuclear polarization, the nuclear spins can be phase-locked to this internal electronic field. This breakthrough opens pathways for building solid-state quantum memories with enhanced controllability.
main_problem: To achieve coherent control over nuclear spin ensembles without relying on external phase references, which is crucial for scalable quantum memory.
main_result: The internal electronic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can be utilized to deterministically phase-lock the nuclear spins, enabling measurement of their coherence and precession using only internal couplings.
method: The study combines experimental measurements on silicon quantum dots with detailed numerical simulations of the electron-nuclear many-body system dynamics.
model_or_system: The platform is a double quantum dot in silicon hosting coupled electronic spins (S-T transitions) and nuclear spins ($	ext{}^{29}	ext{Si}$). The physics involves coupling between the electron spin, the SOC term ($u$), and the hyperfine interaction ($\Delta HF$).
key_observables: Coherent precession of nuclear spins, inhomogeneous dephasing time ($T_2^*$), and the electronic transition probability $\langle P_T angle$ as a function of wait times ($t_w$) or evolution time ($t$).
important_parameters: External magnetic fields ($	ext{B}_{	ext{ext}}$), SOC strength ($u$), hyperfine coupling ($\Delta HF$), and the ratio between these couplings.
main_assumptions: The analysis sometimes treats nuclei as classical spins for Hamiltonian derivation, and simulations account for various noise sources (e.g., white magnetic noise).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how SOC modifies polarization regions; subsequent figures show time evolution of $\langle P_T angle$ vs. $t_w$, demonstrating the stroboscopic screening effect when $t_w$ matches the Larmor period, and finally plot coherence decay envelopes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for internal control to detailing the mechanism (SOC-induced phase locking via screening), quantifying this control by measuring free precession and coherence times, and concluding with a comprehensive analysis of parameter dependence ($u$ vs $\Delta HF$).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete demonstration of using intrinsic material couplings (SOC) as an internal clock or reference field for quantum memory elements, bypassing the need for external microwave infrastructure.
